blocks.content: That glance would have been softer and far more profound, That moment, more exuberant and lively That silence at the backdrop of that transfixed glance, a lot more comforting and golden That embrace must have lasted longer, tighter, melting deep into the soul, the warmth unprecedented the silence and those starry eyes saying it all Those late nights would have been more of gratitude and less of regrets or guilt or any signs of anguish. That warm moist impression on the cheek would have comforted all the sorrows Those fights would have all made sense, and despite the differences, there would be unprecedented bliss in finding more reasons to bond stronger Had we known we would have to wait a little too long? Be a little too far away? And endure it through far darker times? This too shall pass

title: The Circular Butterfly
author: Unknown
preview: It was a typical January evening accompanied by an eerie winter breeze. A crestfallen man trudged along the snow, hunched in the soft moonlight, an aura of paranoia and alertness around him, a war veteran I supposed. He...

blocks.content: It was a typical January evening accompanied by an eerie winter breeze. A crestfallen man trudged along the snow, hunched in the soft moonlight, an aura of paranoia and alertness around him, a war veteran I supposed. He moved briskly but silently, like a predator lurking in the dark, scouring his victim with those two perfect yellow eyes. Dark chased light as the final rays of hope vanished into the night and the man seemed to disappear with it.

My day had been a weird one, albeit the fact they all have the same level of monotony around them but today was especially weird. I looked at the scene with interest particularly because the mystery around the character impulsively induced a feeling of déjà vu. I couldn’t place it then and it didn’t seem to matter because I had a perfectly good gaming system set up inside my safe haven, considering how I was made to sit through the screening of The Butterfly Effect. The only thing that had piqued my attention today had left, that ancient trophy wading through the trail.

The cold wind made me realise I had left my jacket on the couch, and on top of that there was no one at the door. This was frustrating. In all of my rage of being called without any reason and my dreams of playing football professionally, I threw the cola can high into the air. It matched the sun on its trajectory and I returned before it could hit the road.

I opened my eyes. I knew it was my job to pry out of the cryo chamber immediately, but the sleep had taken its toll on my physicality. My first impulse was to throw up. Alarms blared in the distance, lights flashing around, but everything was in a daze. I remember thinking about how beautiful life seemed but I had a job to do. I rushed to the bridge. My training had taught me that this situation meant death but how does one give up on hope. Experimental missions have their own chances at risk, mostly those that are off the books too. We were never supposed to return but in the chaos and flames, I could not figure out what went haywire. If I couldn’t have saved the ship then no one could have. I turned to Camera 12A to see the calm expressions on the faces of my crew. I frantically hit the buttons, and in the process thanked them for their service. Then everything went white, a symphony played in the background as I went to sleep again.

Blood flowed through the drains. The rain only added to the mess. Bullet shells on the field and a few policemen interspersed with bullets, catching their last breaths. Over at the place where the inmate escaped was the body of a prisoner stabbed in the throat. A walkie-talkie switched from static to signal, “Inmate AG567 escaped custody today. Be advised subject is extremely dangerous and highly delusional, considers himself to be a little girl. Send ambulances over to the scene. Four dead and 3 critical in the escape carried out. The subject and accomplices escaped in an ice cream van, I repeat, an ice cream van.”
The cola reached the peak of its trajectory and landed on the sidewalk, with a single person to witness the event who kept his pace on.

Unaware of his surroundings, well lost in his thoughts, the strange looking man with a strange sounding name tripped on the can. He hit the sidewalk hard, cursed his fate and got up in pain. He resolved to confront the perpetrator and followed him to his house. The person invited himself in to give him a piece of his mind. After about a minute of a heated argument, presumably over a can but more accurately over the ethics and procedure of can throwing, he noticed the resident’s gaming set-up. It promised the quintessential change in technology, major modifications never seen before, running a game no one had ever heard of before. He asked to be let in to study it in a greater detail. Closer inspection revealed almost fantastic research ideas, exquisite modified setups, proper codes and exceptional innovation. The resident was the perfect candidate for the CONSILIUM mission. The person, a professor, invited the resident to become a part of the space confidentiality, to lead a mission off the books, something so extravagant such that it could not be defined in normal terms. The professor knew that he was rushing things even after a couple years of training but it was essential to do so.

I took the lead of the CONSILIUM mission. I did not know the exact purpose. Rather no one knew, everyone knew only parts of the final solution, compartmentalisation we called it. It gave me the opportunity to get out of the house and maybe as cheesy as it sounds, to use my abilities to my potential. As we got into Earth’s orbit, all everyone had was second thoughts. We were never going to return again. The professor had chosen all of us as we had nothing to do and would rather be part of something rather than sit alone at home. It had worked. He was pretty successful in setting up a team and we had embarked on our mission. I still didn’t know the purpose behind the mission. We were promised all answers when we reached Europa, the place where we would finally understand the mission that was apparently supposed to be the most important mission till date, something so confidential that even the team involved could not be trusted with the information let alone the general public. Bubbling with curiosity we all entered cryo sleep.
Little did I know.

I opened my eyes again. This time in a stark white room. It was a mental asylum. 3 years had passed since the crash. I was not supposed to be alive but one cannot mess with causality. The doctors explained to me the events that had happened, how the mission failed, how the crew died. How PTSD and vertigo were to be my defining traits now. Therapy and Counselling outlined my day.
Those times were tough.
But they were happy to me.
I played in the garden, under the sun and shade, on top of trees and hiding throughout the space. I felt joy in that space.
I learnt a new word in those days.
“Schizophrenia”
Years passed.
And people thought that I was going to be completely okay.
Little did they know.

The next time I opened my eyes again was in a different garden. I was introduced to my parents. I liked them. I stayed there for years I think. But I craved some ice-cream. I guess they did too. Because they fell to the ground in joy when they were showered with the rainbow sprinkles. I felt proud. I got on the van and we left riding on a rainbow towards my dreams.
Finally Free.

I lost my garden that day. The man dropped me off at a house. I didn’t see a garden rather a house that felt my own. I looked back, wondering where I was these past few years. I turned back. The ice cream man was the professor, the same guy who had given me the job. How strange to have snapped out of it.
What was the word again?
“Schizophrenia”
Had it ended, I didn’t really care.
I asked the professor about the mission and how it had failed.
“It did work exactly how it was supposed to.” The professor said.
I didn’t understand. Maybe my confused expression demanded an explanation.
“I know you don’t understand. But realise, remember, comprehend, scrutinise this, Time is now circular.”
I looked into the mirror. I was an old man now. I looked exactly like the professor.
He asked me out on a movie. I agreed.
“The Butterfly Effect.”
What an utter piece of crap it was.
I returned back home, trudging along the snow. It was a typical January evening accompanied by an eerie winter breeze.

I noticed someone staring at me from across the road. A can of cola in his hand. I looked at the scene with interest particularly because the mystery around the character impulsively induced a feeling of déjà vu…

title: The Cola Can
author: Unknown
preview: 27 January 2037,10:27 p.m., Monday. It’s been 17 years since I have been watching the pale moon shine on the clouds and clustered leaves print their shadows on the walls that surround me. The night being as cold as it al...

blocks.content: 27 January 2037,10:27 p.m., Monday. It’s been 17 years since I have been watching the pale moon shine on the clouds and clustered leaves print their shadows on the walls that surround me. The night being as cold as it always was, reminding me every night of how cold the world is out there. Every night, the sound of the wind breezing past the iron rust slowly decays me, cell by cell. The walls witnessing how I have been broken and shattered all through these years. They might be the only one’s who would remember my existence after I join the moon and the stars in the cold nights that I live through every night. Little did I know that someday, I would not be a part of anyone’s memory and that these red bricks that make the wall around me would be the only part of the world that would ever know that I was. 17 long years, of me watching the moon rise on me each night, as if it looks at me in pity. This long a time would suffice to kill any thoughts a person could ever have. 17 years, is long enough to kill of all memories of a person and I might also say that it takes 17 Years for a soul to decay till its end. 17 years ago, my nights ended with ice cream for the family and dinner with Alan saying grace. Alan, my youngest son, used to love saying grace before meals for he had just learnt to do so in school. Julia, my wife would have for us a lovely meal prepared to finish off our days and we were the happiest families in the royal lineage. Our lives were everything anyone could ever wish for. I had respect in people’s heart and love from everyone that knew me. Little did I know that those were the last days of me knowing that such a thing would exist. I was sent here for a murder, a murder I didn’t commit but I suppose the world conspired to pin it down on me. A murder that took away the respect I had earned in all the years I had grown up, it took away the pride people had when they identified themselves to me and it took away my world, it took my Alan and my Julia. A murder that left me in here with these walls and with moonlight every night that have slowly and slowly killed off all my thoughts and all my memories. All these years, and the only memory I have left is what haunts me each day and each night. It breaks me up and shatters me to the very core. The words ring in my ears when I try to close my eyes and they seem to be taunting me when I’m awake. The sentence that ended my life as I knew it and brought me to a place where I decay each moment. “The Court of Victoria finds Prince Robert to be guilty of adultery and murder of one, Elena Kosch, and orders that his name be struck off him all record book and that his involvement with any part of the United Kingdom be removed from existence. The court also sentences Robert to a life term imprisonment in the Waldor Prison.”

8 February 2020, 3:36 p.m., Saturday. After Robert addresses the people of Anfield, all of us come home to sit together and talk like a family after a long time. Robert has been away from home for the past few months and Alan is delighted to be with his father this time around. “Dad, do you know how to mould clay?” He keeps asking Robert, but somehow somewhere, I have a feeling that Robert is in a different sphere. He seems a little disconnected from us this time around. It probably might just be the jet lag or that coming home might be a change to him from all the travelling he has been doing. Anyway, I brush aside this thought, knowing that being with the family will bring him back to us, back to his home. Tonight, we host a homecoming dinner for Robert, and everyone who knows him since he has been growing up is invited. The gala begins and all of our guests are delighted to see Robert in the flesh. He is center of attention tonight, and I guess he deserves it too. Watching him smile with his old friends makes me happy. I haven’t seen his smile in months and this is what I cherish the most about him. His smile. As I head to have myself a drink, Mona finds me and pulls me into a corner. She has an urgency in her eyes and somehow, she is screaming even before she has uttered a word. “There is something you must know”. There is a panic and fear in her which has me scared. And this is when everything falls apart for me and breaks me down. She says, “Robert, Robert has done something bad”. I nervously ask her to sit but she just wants to blurt something out. “Did you hear about the murder in Scotland a week ago, a girl, in her 20s was killed?”. I had not known of such an incident but this didn’t really bother me at first as I thought it was out of context. The next sentence she says chills my spine and has me frozen, “Robert was staying there too and its him who murdered her.” “The girl, Elena, had met Robert when he was in Ukraine, and she was travelling with him for all these past months. It was on the streets all over Eastern Europe that Robert was seen with a young girl in all his tours and visits. It was quite evident that they were having an affair and that Robert, when he got to Scotland, figured that if the people of United Kingdom found out about this, he’d lose everything and he had to anyhow get rid of Elena before he reached back home at Anfield”. Before I can comprehend what she just said, she shows me a tape of Robert with the girl and shows me a couple of photos of them having dinner. This makes my heart stop and breaks me down. Tears leave my eyes but I somehow hold them back. I hold onto my wits and I know that I’ll make Robert pay for this. The next morning, I make sure everything reaches the press and the next day, I have Robert in court. I make sure everything is done to erase off every memory of Robert that any of us would ever have. And I bury him in the jails once and for all.

24 October 2019, 6:38 p.m., Thursday I met Mona on one of my visits to London for selling the drugs I had smuggled from Africa. She seemed to be in a mood to strike a deal with me ever since we made eye contact. I knew that she might be a truckload of trouble but I also knew that she could bring me a truckload of money. So, it didn’t come to me as a shock when she asked to find a girl that would love to travel and would be into selling my drugs to someone important. I knew Elena was the one girl who I could rely on. I had brought her into this business just so that I could rake in the big bucks that someone like Mona could offer me for such a job. And I knew Elena could never say no to me given that I had provided her with a new means to life when she had nothing to hold onto and was shattered to pieces. Elena had readily agreed to do the job, after all, it involved drugs, travelling across Europe and one fine English Gentleman, it didn’t have to take much convincing to get her to agree to this. I knew that this was my chance at getting as rich as my the next three of my generations needed to be and the deal was done. Elena went to meet with the fine Englishman, and Mona had wired me all the cash I needed to swim in money for ages to come.

12 June 2018,3:42 a.m,Saturday Elena is staring at herself while she contemplates whether it’s worth living anymore or not. She looks at her own eyes , they have been red and bloody after all the crying she has done the whole night. On top of that some asshole has just spilled an entire cola ,while she was walking down the street, on her favourite jacket. She hurried to the bathroom hoping that maybe she could undo the damage. “You do know this is a Men’s Room right?” said a voice from the corner. She was startled but she didn’t want to show it. And then he started flirting, getting too close like all men.. but something about him was different. He had some sort of a charm unlike others. She had been dating Aaron for the past year but somehow, that night, Liam made her smile a bit more than she usually does. He appreciated the spark in her eyes and played with her hair while she giggled. She hadn’t felt this way in a long time and she felt like there was something in Liam that pulled her towards him. The walk back to her place led to one thing and another and before they knew it, they were both into each other, somehow leaving behind what anyone else would think of them and were just making out like there was no tomorrow. This moment, this very moment is the time when Aaron opens the door to find Elena on top of another man. He doesn’t think a lot but the only thing he does at this very moment is slams the lamp on Liam’s head and keeps doing so till there is blood all over. He slaps Elena so hard she drops down cold. He slams the door on his way out and leaves Elena bludgeoned and Liam, almost dead. This leaves Elena in the middle of the night, with no person to talk to her and nothing to help her out of her misery. This brings her to something she never thought would get into, but she does. She finds help in drugs that she bought out of curiosity. She keeps doing drugs till she is left with nothing but an addiction to it. This brings about desperate times for her and this is when she gets into the drug smuggling business.

11 June 2018,9: 54p.m, Friday Me and my friends had just watched this movie, “The Butterfly Effect”, and damn, it was just some far fetched drama to make a story out of thin air. People in the movies business seem to think that they could create content out of absolutely nothing and believe that the audience would buy the crap that they hope to sell in the name of a “Butterfly Effect”. My friend is completely on board with the movie and he says ”The Butterfly effect isn’t just that small things have big consequences , it means that each and every creature on this planet is connected through our actions whether e are aware or not.” but I don’t think I could ever fathom such logic. I mean, who on earth would believe that say, Suppose I spill this cola I have in my hands, the world would end? At this moment, I stop to give a shit and throw the damn cola can into the air. Some of it spills on this young girl in her 20s…, I apologise immediately for what I did but she just screams “asshole” and starts running to the washroom. She was probably in a hurry because she went into the men’s room.
I could’ve stopped her… but I didn’t

title: The Butterfly Effect
author: Unknown
preview: Butterfly effect or the chaos theory dictates that in a system defined by non linear equations, even a microscopic change in the initial data can lead to unpredictable and often cataclysmic changes in the outcome. The de...

blocks.content: Butterfly effect or the chaos theory dictates that in a system defined by non linear equations, even a microscopic change in the initial data can lead to unpredictable and often cataclysmic changes in the outcome. The degree, however, depends on how far from the initiation we take the outcome to be. There is in fact a lot of scientific mumbo jumbo in the aforementioned words but not nearly enough to capture the true essence and brilliance of what is. To bring things into perspective, the name sake of this effect, a butterfly flapping its wings can be the reason a hurricane is born a thousand miles away. Such beauty, such deliverance is real reason why the world works the way it does. I, for one, am in awe with the higher powers at work here. I appreciate what is and almost feel bad for the people who don’t. This right here is therefore an attempt to justify why it’s not ‘utter crap’. Doesn’t matter how futile, but an attempt nevertheless. An ode to that unsuspecting butterfly.

We all have an understanding of the term ‘aftereffect’, lets try to figure out what was before that butterfly flapped its wings. The answer is simple, there was a butterfly. How that butterfly came to be? You might ask and brownie points for asking that because that, precisely, is the point of it all. There is always something that lead to the way things are in this exact moment.

I am not going to pretend that I have a fair understanding of how anything works because frankly, I do not. Your guess is as good as mine, but hey, I was told to be creative. And why everything pans out the way it does, maybe we’ll never know but trying is the most we can do, so try we shall.

It’s pointless turning back the clock, searching for the reasons that transpired this event of me trying to convince you that there is indeed something that we fail to see, for this is as old as time itself. The point is, we are here, alive, kicking, thinking, writing and all because at some point in this infinite continuum of time and space, something was at the right place at the right time. I mean look around you, everything is right where it should be, no more no less. It seems almost impossible and yet, here we are, conscious of ourselves and our thoughts. Just enough to realize the fact that we are unique and for a reason that are still incomprehensible to us.

Humans have this innate ability to associate meaning to everything. That is how the concept of religion was born, people trying to pin the wonder of life to an entity watching over us, deliberating events that lead to an average planet, revolving around a very average star. Trying to give meaning to chaos, and chaos it is, such a beautiful one.

The Chaos theory, to me, is anything but chaos. I believe there is reason to everything is and turns out to be the way it does. Even the most menial of things, water, for example. It’s most dense at 4 degree Celsius, not zero, not any other number but four, for a reason that I will not mention in the interest of our time and ability to tolerate details. Not only that but there are elements and phenomenon that take place with pin point precision, so much so that even a miniscule change would render life impossible and yet we live without a care in the world and everything just takes care of itself. It’s hard not to involve a higher power. The reason, however, still unknown.

There is just so much beauty around that it almost frustrating that we don’t know who to credit it for. The Butterfly Effect. Maybe it indeed is bullsh*t, complete coincidences piling up and hence, our desperate attempts to pin meaning to something that might not even be there. Theorizing, contemplating, pondering for countless hours instead of doing something that is just as pointless.

All of this makes me wonder what is the point of it all and eventual nihilism but it’s only justified. Everything you do can be followed up with a ‘why?’ or a ‘what?’ till a point comes where you can no longer justify existence and yet we don’t give up. We strive, we fail, we learn, we laugh, we love and we write. In the grand scheme of things, does it even matter if I write something that you will love or hate? But I write nevertheless. I express myself to a degree that almost annoys you but I ask myself how does it matter in the grand scheme of things and all is well again.

All is well because I am here and I can think of all the chaos that lead me to this…realization. The realization that maybe everything does happen for a reason and there is indeed a higher power or maybe there isn’t an we are just floating away on a rock with no certain tomorrow. We’d like to think that we are in control and that is what we are taught from the very beginning. Maybe it is the case, maybe it isn’t. Bottom line is, we need to make peace with it and carry on. Pondering upon the purpose and possibilities. Trying to answer the questions that may not have an answer. Seeking purpose, meaning and eventual but eternal happiness.

You see, everything that you do can be boiled down to happiness. And what exactly is it? Happiness? To your disappointment (and mine as well) it’s just dopamine being released in your brain. How shallow does that make you feel? That everything you do is to convince your brain to release an indifferent arrangement of molecules?

So, the Butterfly Effect, what is it? I believe it’s just a distraction we created for ourselves to justify our actions that in totality have no consequences. Something we coined to keep us from insanity.
The end?

title: A Con-fusing Choice
author: Unknown
preview: I woke up to the sound of an old man yelling “TRAMP” nearby, probably outside one of the rooms was the scene of alcohol, disappointment and rejection that night. It was 5:30 in the morning and as I looked out of the wind...

blocks.content: I woke up to the sound of an old man yelling “TRAMP” nearby, probably outside one of the rooms was the scene of alcohol, disappointment and rejection that night. It was 5:30 in the morning and as I looked out of the window of my cheap motel room, I could see the blood-stained sun piercing through the snowy haze who somehow managed to do his job daily and remained perfectly stationary, without ever deviating. My job had its ups and downs, sure. I was extremely rich because as it unsurprisingly turns out if your job has to deal with the deepest, darkest secrets of prominent businessmen, celebrities and politicians, they keep your wallet full. On the flip side though, my job requires, above all, anonymity. So the commonality between my exquisite travels to Vegas, Geneva or New Delhi was always that stinking cheap motel. Also, and this is a big one according to most humans, I don’t have any friends or a romantic counterpart. I can’t form attachments when I am working a case and I don’t think people are willing to date a con master who will be at home for three weeks in a year. I do have an agent though because I am terrible at organisational work. I know him as noob_master69. We talk a lot but I don’t think I’m going to ask him out. Honestly, he’s a bore.

I slipped into my slippers as I rose from my bed and picked up my phone. Notifications later, I thought as I Googled “Hangover cure to keep me active all day”. I think every website was in purple but I don’t remember ever making or drinking one. There’s a first time for everything, right? When you grow up conning people for a living, concoctions aren’t really a primary concern. My career started when I was 14, I think? My best friend in school, Anirudh, asked me to figure out whether or not his crush was single. I don’t remember the exact details of it but I do remember excelling at conning people and at disappointing the ones closest to me, and the immense joy. Thanks to my Anirudh, I now had a new hobby. And for a young master conman living in the slums of Bombay, life was good. I worked my way up from lowly thugs to Mumbai’s most elite. I worked on my flirtation skills, presentation skills and imitations. I watched movies, TV shows and I idolized DiCaprio’s character from Catch Me If You Can. For a boy whose mother died while delivering him, and whose father never held on to a job long enough to actually be able to spend some quality time at home with his son, and whose teachers probably didn’t have teachers, a moral compass doesn’t exist. It’s survival, food, glamour on one side and on the other, rotting in a slum.

As I thought about all this, I probably ended up overbrushing my teeth. It was 6:30 am and I had to postpone the hangover cure to some other day. Obviously I had work to do, at least that was what my alarm was screaming at that moment but more importantly, something unexpected happened that almost, literally, blew my mind.

My phone burst into flames at 6:31 am, sharp. I don’t think I could have crafted a better concoction, honestly. For a cheap motel, this one had surprisingly superb fire alarm systems. Water was everywhere and my ears were ringing as I jumped out of the window into the

beautiful city of Oslo with whatever I could grab. First things first, let’s analyse what happened. Someone tried to kill me-police is going to investigate the explosion so I need a new identity and new getup- someone tried to blow my head off- I was at the bar in the city last night charming Ms Medha for a case presented to me by the Indian arms dealer Mr Pulkit Deshmukh for a surprisingly massive amount of money, not that I mind – I don’t remember much which is weird because I know how to handle my alcohol-someone tampered with my phone and tried to blow my fucking head off. I entered a taxi, got off at a thrift store, changed my getup and walked over to a PCO. I dialled noob_master69’s emergency-only number and gave him a quick summary. I was rewarded with a list of concise instructions. 1) Get a burner phone 2) Print out your new ID at a cybercafe 3)Reverse engineer what happened at the bar, or jump countries ASAP 4) You will have everything I can dig up on Deshmukh and Medha in 15 minutes on your mail 5) Be loyal, do not say anything about your agent no matter what happens now. I only needed him for (1) and (3) honestly.

After a quick breakfast at a cafe cafe, I bought a phone and proceeded to the cyber cafe. Step 1, check. Step 2, check. I am now Orfuk Vladimir, a bartender who does part-time shifts at various bars and pubs. I was never one to back down from a fight so I read everything noob had on Deshmukh and Medha on my cab ride to the CCD bar, in the heart of the city. Convincing the one guy working his lonely morning shift to go out and something worthwhile with his limited hours on Earth while I cover for his job was a piece of cake. Now, onto business. I tried to relive that night and trace the explosion to its origin. The booth I sat at, the drinks I ordered, the people around me- everything was a blur except Ms Medha. I had to interrogate her, but how? My eyes fell on something on the billing computer at the counter. A name I hadn’t seen for years. ‘CCD Bar, a holding of Ojha Pvt Ltd’. Anirudh Ojha, could it really be him? Before I had time to react properly, I got my answer. A guy entered the bar. He was of average build and height, he had ruffled hair and an unshaven beard. It was him, only the last time I saw him, he wasn’t pointing a gun at my face. Medha walked in right behind him.

“Hey Ojha,” I said with a smile. “Hey, Banga. Wait sorry, who are you right now?” “A bartender, I see your observation skills never improved” “Shut up!” “Okay then, no pleasantries. What the heck is going on?” “I do not want to shoot you unless you prompt me to” “That’s reassuring” “I and Medha are the current associate heads of the ELS syndicate in Mumbai, the syndicate that brought you to where you are right now. We’ve been tracking you for two years now” “I don’t need a history lesson but hey, congrats on the promotion. At least you won’t go around pulling the trigger for someone anymore. You’ll be the one ordering hits” “Don’t act like you’re a saint. The things you’ve done might not seem as cruel to you because you’ve never observed the consequences, have you?” “What do you mean?” “You’ve caused deaths and crushed dreams Ankur, countless, and no these aren’t the ones you won’t care about.”

“You’ve been working for the HSS for the past few years” cut in Medha, interrupting the soon-to-be melodramatic best friend reunion. “The same HSS that is the reason that kids in Mumbai slums never rise high enough to see a clear sky and drives the income inequality to a much worse state. Before you object, I have a folder full of your cases and I can explain to you why every single one has strengthened the HSS in ways you never expected. Hence, I had no option but to drug you, render you completely inactive, rig your phone and hope you die. You clearly defied my expectations ”

“Thank You?” I said, my eyes wide open. “I wasn’t aware of all that. Sorry. I know you won’t do it on purpose, nothing can corrupt you to this extent. I know you’ll never betray your origins, or me. You still regret what happened all those years ago.” My heart skipped a beat. “So in 5 minutes, figure out how this could happen and I won’t have to shoot you in the head.” finished Ojha. I couldn’t believe this was happening. It was too much to process. “It’s too much to process!” I exclaimed as I found a seat to support me. I felt the gun stashed behind me rub up against my butt as I considered my options. Shooting my way out was an idiotic option, Ojha was an experienced marksman and I couldn’t have taken him even if he was there alone. So I started paying heed to what they said, and I thought. I thought between my best friend who I grew up with and the only person I talk to often. I had never faced such a difficult decision, ever before. But then again, it was Anirudh, always Anirudh. At the end of 5 minutes, all I could force out of my throat was “noob_master69”. “What?” asked Anirudh “He handles all my cases. He tells me what case to take on, and he arranges everything” I explained. “You must have contacted him as Mr Deshmukh, I presume?” “Yes,” said Medha, still giving me that creepy look of mistrust. “Well then that’s it!” exclaimed Ojha. “All we need to do is figure out a way which enables Ankur here to con his partner on the job, figure out his identity and eliminate him, if need be.” “It’s not going to be easy. He’s smart and he knows me. Also, I don’t know if my heart is in this given that you just tried to kill me” “Well then your heart can be stopped,” said Medha. “Hey, relax. Keep your weapon aside. Ankur, do it for me. Trust me.” said Ojha, looking me in the eye. “Okay.”

Medha’s tech guys started working on whatever lead noob’s emergency number could lead to as I and Ojha got some time to catch up in the bar’s office. We went from small talk to general life to wavering around the elephant in the room to the elephant. “So that job, all those years ago. You’re right, I regret it.”

“Hey don’t beat yourself over it. We all make mistakes” said Ojha. “It was a lot more than some simple mistake, I got careless. I never realized that my carelessness could lead to you being in danger.” “Hey come on I-”

“No! I almost got you killed. That’s the reason I don’t make any attachments anymore. I just cannot take the risk. And even now if what you say is true I’ve been doing the very actions I swore against?! Everything I’ve done will always haunt me now, forever” I screamed as I held back my tears.

Anirudh walked up to me, held me and put his lips to mine. It felt nice. It felt like everything I’ve been doing for the past few years was useless if I didn’t have that. It felt like home and money never gave me that. It reminded me of our childhood together, and that was worth more than all my cons combined. Medha walked in. “We have something”

I was briefed. The call logs on that number led to the house of a high profile financial trader living in Bombay. We went over the plan on the flight. It was my most challenging deception yet. I had to finalize every minute detail. There was something about the smell of my city that made my adrenaline kick in. If there ever was someone who could do this, it was me. I arrived at his high rise apartment disguised as a member of the HSS. I had to pretend to offer him more insider information for more money or some weird permutation of the same, assuming that there was a similar deal in place. It was extremely risky, and it could have gone very wrong, any second. Thankfully, it didn’t go wrong enough. He did figure out I was conning him but he had uttered what we needed by then in the following snapshot of our conversation, “….” “I think Athale would have notified me of this change” “….” The poor trader obviously disappeared. Parth Athale was one of the heads of the HSS. The pieces were falling into place, I made the correct decision. I had the chance to right my every wrong. The only thing left was to draw him out into the open. A simple news flash that the trader’s body was found in a discrete location was enough to ambush Athale. I witnessed it all. I witness how Athale’s bodyguards were shot down, how Medha and Ojha pointed their guns right at Athale’s forehead, I remember the final look Athale gave me. He looked decent and he had curly hair. I could see his eyes through the specs he wore. More than anger or betrayal, I think Athale’s look told me I made a mistake. It was sheer disappointment. I don’t know, did I do the right thing? I picked one evil out of the two, but is picking the lesser evil, that too in my perspective, up to me? What is God for? My allegiance didn’t shift from Anirudh even though I worked with Athale for 20 years. I chose love and home more than simple loyalty, I thought as I played his final instructions over and over in my head. Lucky for you, there’s no cliffhanger here. Because Ojha turned around, walked towards me, gun in his hand and said, “Let’s get drunk tonight.” Which we did. We slept together. In the morning, as Ojha was leaving my room he said, “You know we will need your skills right? I am the new noob master. You will get the other details soon.” I finally made the hangover cure that morning, but I made one change to the top recipe. A tablespoon of the deadliest poison I had. I don’t think I’m going back to loyalty after playing for the home side. More than I feared his bullet, I feared his absence in my life.

title: The Ticket, the Jacket, and the Can
author: Unknown
preview: Chaos, it is what God wants or maybe we do or perhaps believe that He wants. Who are we to say anyway? He created us in his image or did We? Alright this is a…a…..a detour, come back, there is a story about to occur and...

blocks.content: Chaos, it is what God wants or maybe we do or perhaps believe that He wants. Who are we to say anyway? He created us in his image or did We? Alright this is a…a…..a detour, come back, there is a story about to occur and you do not want to be a part of any philosophical derailing, I mean discourse. Remember, this is not happening just because you are reading this. This is the second coming of Valmiki but the author has died, as Barthes wanted.

It was a great day, a red sky, making the pale french girls look like they were blushing, maybe they were. A hot day with an imminent chilly wind, a messenger of the winter, riffed a few beats through the fiery locks of my old love. We were on the way back from that over-aged film, “The Butterfly Effect”, our first one together back in the golden days, as they are for everyone. Looking back at it, it was a shitty pact to rewatch it after more than a decade. So much that we just crushed the tickets like we wanted to…ummm…. and tossed it away into the woods. It seemed to resemble the stale and wrinkling bond we now had, as the Man already said, “Bare laid the ruins, where late the sweet birds sang”. He said a lot, correction, wrote a lot and still managed to be true, truer than the phoenix’s tears which couldn’t heal the ravaged heart which somehow managed to beat inside. This storm of thoughts went on and I stopped for a drink, nothing better than an icy coke and rum to cool off and heat up. Got the singular red and a cask of rum to go, a can too much. The drink worked its miracle, although the signature red can wasn’t dry and it just had to get on my jacket, thanks to the stupid bitch who always finds a way to fuck it all up.

As I said, it was getting cold, a jacket became a necessity and I just Kobe’ed the can into the trashcan before trotting off into the nearest store I could see which just had to be the very same one where I bought this ruined jacket with this witch. You get me, right? I am sure you do. I bought the exact same one so it goes along well with the rest. I could be lucky because it was the last piece they had, nothing more would ever be made. Sometime later, someone else, somebody higher up, walked into the store to get a jacket. Well, you know what’s next, great men think alike and consequently, wear alike but it was out of the bounds of heavens for him.

The next day he went cold to his fancy office, worked up and trying to warm his hands by blowing into his interlocked fists. A sort out day’s work ahead piled in front, he started to work his way through it. The clock went round, time off and the mechanism’s works. It is a regular day by all means, nothing much apart from the seldom tense air which was glowing that day. A mistake had been made, nothing much. just a misplaced punctuation, That’s all. Obviously, it was the cold man. There’s more to it, the file was to be sent to the Queen. Yes, this is where it blows up. The can finds its way to contribute, to find its meaning. Aluminium can be a catalyst to a great many organic reactions, as if it wants to. It finds its way to the land of cheap labour, sorry, world’s manufacturing backbone to be recycled and given a new purpose. It works its wonders
instead. Brings about a chemical reaction which alters the DNA in just the right way to end a third of the population the world across.

Fun fact: tickets are usually printed on thermal paper as opposed to those hard stubs there were in the Golden Age of Hollywood. It’s in the details, you will see. The tickets flew in the breeze until it all curled up into a heap with dry leaves. Now, the thing with dry leaves of the species found in the area is they burst up and thermal paper catches sparks quite readily. Hot day, dry leaves, thermal paper, is this a conspiracy or what? Fire broke out in the area and is nature’s doing, nothing more. Well, humans are nature and vice versa, after all. It has been months since the fire now, hopefully it will soon go off due to the blast. Wait, it’s not a blast, it’s the blow of the horn at dusk. Humanity’s dusk.

This is, my friend, the miracle of language. A single punctuation or grammatical error and English go haywire. Now, what does the heavy crown do when it lazily rests on a head all its life? It blocks the flow of blood to the brain. Now, this is a nice thing for someone to write on. Behold, a monarch with hindered cognitive abilities, meets a fun orangutan and they have tea in the middle of one of the most detailed to be awfully boring house. And she bobs her head sleepily into the tea. The documents to be honoured with their signatures are brought in and they mindlessly do it as they are. The errors are exploited and the video games are played.

When exactly are you, you might be wondering. Now is where you are, a wild-wild wildfire, a big red button begging to be pushed and an unstoppable virus just out there. So, who is responsible, Lorenz? Satan? It is you. How else would I know what the cold man did, where the breeze took the tickets, why are societies hierarchical.

title: “Oceans Rise, Empires Fall”
author: Unknown
preview: Darkness fell over the earth. The floor beneath split in perfect unison with the skies. A cloth somewhere tore. Knees fell to the ground. “Surely these were a righteous people.” I was shaken but oddly indifferent also. I...

blocks.content: Darkness fell over the earth. The floor beneath split in perfect unison with the skies. A cloth somewhere tore. Knees fell to the ground. “Surely these were a righteous people.” I was shaken but oddly indifferent also. I saw the world as one would in a moving bus with its aisle lights on: the truth of what I was feeling overshadowing the world as it really was; without a careful focus on the reflection of the inside of the bus, or on the world outside, all one sees is a superposition of both – which is the truth of neither reality.

Through the collapse of the empire I lived through memories I was aware would hold power over me, even as they were being made, long after the people in them drifted away. The clock struck three. The last of the empire went up in flames. I wasn’t sure if it was okay for me to stand up then, so I continued to kneel. The sun would come out soon, and then I would know. The smoke was so thick, and the fires so wild that not too much ahead was visible.
The foundations of the empire had been my foundation for so long.

I tried to remember the succession of events as they had been before the collapse. The only thing that came to mind was a certain cock’s crow. I decided instead to focus on life as it might be with a collapsed empire. Was it survival instincts that insisted I run? I didn’t acknowledge the shame that accompanied that thought. There wasn’t much sense in moaning its death anyway.

The sun came out just in time to shed light on the empire breathing its last. A sudden downpour of rain washed away the already starving flames. The view from outside the compounds was chilling in its unfamiliarity.
I made a silent wish with regard to the spirits of the empire and the heavens above. And then I stood up, dusted my knees, and walked away.

title: Mid-Week Musings
author: Unknown
preview: I don’t generally write in a ‘non-poetic’ way; never felt the need to do so, but oh well… what is the world if not an array of unexpected uncontemplated disorder? I haven’t said much yet and its already serendipitously s...

blocks.content: I don’t generally write in a ‘non-poetic’ way; never felt the need to do so, but oh well… what is the world if not an array of unexpected uncontemplated disorder?

I haven’t said much yet and its already serendipitously satisfying. So I sit here outside the Café of my college campus, sipping my black coffee but for the most part, unheedingly gazing at the deep black depth of my awakening in a cup.

I have got an important exam tomorrow, but I had one yesterday too. What’s new I wonder. My brain is used to a deep rooted, almost as old as me vice, that of not answering its own questions, and so I drift away into deep thought, just as blank as my answer script is going to be tomorrow.

Its bewildering as to how less I really care or am worried about these exams for which everyone around me seems to be cramming their asses out. Lost as I am, oblivious to human presence around me, I embrace the soft touch of the soothing winter air under the sun. The trees dance as if trying to match the rhythm of the wind as my thoughts resonate in my mind and are slowly attenuated giving way to others like them.

I silently look around me, scrutinising every bit of nature as I turn my head from left to right. Just 180 degrees. A couple in a distance staring at their books and then staring at each other. A smile runs across their faces. Now staring at me, staring at them. Cute. I shift my focus to the trees next to them as I turn my head around slowly admiring and falling in love with the pink and orange and purple flowers on these trees. Still trying to match the rhythm of the wind. ‘Nature never gives up’ I sigh. A broken window, of a dark room tries to tell me a story as it takes me back to the snaps of my own childhood. Running around in the house, innocent, carefree, wild. Running away from studying and getting scolded by a frowning mother. Well that is one thing that hasn’t changed since then I suppose, except for the frowning mother part. Never had I thought as a kid how much care is there behind that frown.
“Sir, your croissant.”
I snap out of my musing as the waiter looks at me as if in a hurry. Maybe he has others to serve.
Eh, when will I finish my coffee? I take a bite of my croissant and drift again.

title: THE KING OF PANDEMONIUM
author: Unknown
preview: Have you ever ventured into roads, Dark and obscure , My fiend heart reigns in them, Malevolent and ugly possessions galore , My pernicious heart trades in them . I stand honored , Setting sadistic paradigm, My virtue is...

blocks.content: Have you ever ventured into roads, Dark and obscure , My fiend heart reigns in them, Malevolent and ugly possessions galore , My pernicious heart trades in them . I stand honored , Setting sadistic paradigm, My virtue is sin, sinister I am. More schadenfreude sentiments slip in . I tempered with the decorum , He showed me his prowess, All I was in the midst of, was my creative process, And I was thrown in dungeon In his momentary triumph, He did foster , in his very holster, The rise of pandemonium. Creative process you beseech? Ever fancied spearheading anarchy? Its zenith hoisted on the tip of….. Gucci! Confession: Needed something to rhyme with, Even the Devil wears Prada you see… So off I went into rebellion , and distressed thronged in the pandemonium , I don’t reminisce realms of happier times, for the simple reason, I’ve never quite had them, Or it might be a queer case of dementia , memory intact , devoid of euphoria…. So I did venture into protest, but alas, luck wasn’t my side that day, my curt father banished me to desert , Which now is beaming with Agonizing frenzy by the way.. And then, Hold your breath , sit and behold , * drum rolls* an interesting anecdote is to unfold, the insinuation bestowed on me , left me dried and parched , because my blood had boiled away in despair, There’s no one to care…. I often mulled over, as the ruler of my clan , what’s it is like to have a concerned glance over the usual scared stares, theres no one who cares…. Your onus might weigh a ton , but standing against your parent is gargantuan , Even for me, also for the Satan., It is no mean feat to rule the pandemonium, By Hades, I mustn’t let loose my fault lines , what if someone taps into them! Ironic no? I would’ve done the same . After all I am the king of pandemonium, a fact of glory albeit quite lame. Though there are times , I do wonder what’s is in the name , what’s in the name?? A story to tell, a secret to hide , I preside those corners where once you’ve cried , Abhor me , I welcome your loathe , Admit , we have all that darker side, gluttony, lust or sheer spite, So why obscure the view , from the blue hue of you? Welcome henceforth, you haven’t such options often, When we’ve got a hell to reign, Why serve in heaven?? title: What If ?
author: Unknown
preview: Sunshine flooded in through the window of a dingy, dusty room as the heavy curtains were pulled to reveal a yellow tinted window. Aaron, a slender man of about 40 spun his eyes through the room, eyeing every aspect with...

blocks.content: Sunshine flooded in through the window of a dingy, dusty room as the heavy curtains were pulled to reveal a yellow tinted window. Aaron, a slender man of about 40 spun his eyes through the room, eyeing every aspect with a look of temptation, mixed with disgust. It had been years since he had set foot in the room. He used to call it genesis or ‘genèse’, reminding him of his elegant primary French teacher, Mademoiselle Alair. What better name for his first office, the origin of his story. As he sat at his desk, the old leather of his chair irked him through his Armani suit. Maybe his old flea market trousers weren’t that bad after all. In the corner of the room lay a pool table, covered with dust but to Aaron, it was the turning point in his life. Every fortune he ever came across in his life could be traced back to that pool table. Or was it misfortune? It was 15 years ago, Aaron Walker was just another budding lawyer in New York City trying out his luck with his partner, Samantha Drew. They had opened shop in an area which was filled with people who needed good legal support but couldn’t afford it. Isn’t that how every lawyer starts? Wanting to do general good for the benefit of the world, secretly hoping that one day they’ll be famous enough to sign on big clients and fill up their pockets. Greed is a natural human instinct, fighting it is of no use. But harnessing that greed in the correct direction might lead to something incredible. Both Samantha and Aaron believed that they had a greed for righteousness, to obtain justice for those who can’t on their own. “Drew & Walker”, they couldn’t possibly have had a better name for it. He had known Samantha since law school, she always struck him as a person who can be reasoned with. Who understands, interprets and then takes action. Important quality for a lawyer. He would have never admitted it but he knew she was a better lawyer than him. She was known throughout the law school for her mock trials, and the lawyer opposite her was known to get completely crushed. She was from a small town in Arizona and had worked hard to admit herself into a prestigious Californian law school. For Aaron, a local of L.A., her views on topics were always a different taste. He loved new perspective on things and he could not have asked for a better partner. You could say she was fair and quite attractive with her flickering green eyes, but Aaron was the ‘business is business’ type of man. They both were smart and genuine people, but why they purchased a second-hand pool table for their office was beyond the comprehension of any person they knew. Some things simply happen, in their own silly manner. It was a simple story.The two were walking around NYC one evening and Samantha became infatuated with a cute squirrel she saw speeding along the street.The squirrel led them to small shop which sold antiquities. Both Aaron and Samantha were attracted to the shop, and the sweet lady at the counter was a master at sales, which is necessity for these small shops. She convinced them both to buy either the pool table or a Mayan statue, and as the reader clearly knows, the pool table was purchased. Every night before heading home, they used to have a game of pool, alive with bets related to the few cases they had. In a few months time, they realized how tough it actually is to be a lawyer in NYC, where in every corner there’s a law firm, and the rent is off the charts. While cutting down on expenses and luxuries they told themselves that were doing this for the good of the public but the fact that they needed a big sum soon was clear as crystal. One rainy evening, the two were in the office fussing over a ruling in a fraud case in 1974, when a burly young man dressed as if he had just come from Hawaii entered with his leaf printed shirt and shorts and a round beige hat. Over the patter of the raindrops on the windowsill he informed the two of his ‘problematic’ situation. “Are you the lawyers?” he said, in a deep harsh voice. Aaron replied in the affirmative. “I will offer you a sum of 10 grand if you help me out in a case” Aaron and Samantha were both extremely shocked. The temptation in them almost brought out the yes but the logic made it stay at the top of the throat. “What kind of a case carries that kind of money with it?” The man replied with a modified offer, “15 grand. And I will only tell you once you take the case, under the confidential agreement. And don’t waste my time, all three of us know you must be in desperate need of money to ‘help people’ “. The exasperation was apparent in his tone. Aaron and Samantha, after much deliberation through the 2 second eye contact they had, agreed. What could possibly be so bad, if they get to help multiple people in return? They would still be retaining their choice to fight his case. The man lay back in his seat, and lit a cigarette without even bothering to ask for permission and began his story. “My name is Todd. I am a business associate of a tech industrialist named Steve Zargenzy.” Aaron’s jaw dropped. Samantha’s face was that of utter shock and disbelief. “I suppose your reactions are justified. He has been all over the news lately. Cheated around tens of thousands of citizens with his ‘cheap but top-notch’ phone. He knew the processors were going to malfunction, but he thought he would be able to handle it. As I am sure you know, he has left the country and gone into hiding with his millions of dollars. And no, I don’t know where, so do not bother asking. See, that’s where I come in, the next-in-line CEO of Zargenzy Tech. We’ll probably change the name” He chuckled to himself. “If you are able to convince the court to lay off the backs of the company and put all the blame on Steve and only Steve, I might actually be able to get the company up on top again. Provide people genuine products. Here’s the case-file. I hope you get the 15 grand” he said with a sort of snort. Something inside of Aaron spoke out. A greedy demon living inside, angry for being neglected so long. “20 grand.” Todd said with a raised eyebrow, “Very well Mr. Walker. I liked the tone.”. With that, he left. Samantha still had a shocked expression, but the newer reason was Aaron. “What are you trying to do? Sell your integrity for 20 grand? Protecting the people cheated in this scam is why we became lawyers. Not protecting the scammers!” Aaron’s response was three-fold. “All the money scammed out of the poor is with Zargenzy in his endless vacation. It’s not coming back. 99% of the employees of Zargenzy Tech probably had no idea about this defect and finding the 1% is impossible. Yes, Todd is a candidate but why not save the jobs of thousands of innocent employees. Also, the amount of good we can do with 20 grand, imagine!” Was that greed a big city origin? No, the devil lives in all of us. Even Samantha nearly crossed the line, but her Arizona childhood resisted her from changing her ways. Even in New York and LA, Arizona never left her. She was not ready to give her dreams up. But even not accepting would lead to that. She went to the case-file and started hunting for a winning point. Both Samantha and Aaron spent three hours and found nothing. Or nothing legal, to be more precise. Aaron had an idea that involved a simple document forging, mostly risk-free, and a high winning chance. But recommending that to Samantha means approaching a lion while wearing a goat-skin. But it was nearly midnight and he had no other option. For a split second after he suggested the idea, Samantha’s eyes seemed to say “I will burn you alive”, slowly changing to “..are you okay?”. Aaron was determined, something had taken over him. And there was only one way he could think of to end this prolonged discussion. Samantha agreed, but said that if she loses, the consequences would be severe. Aaron had no idea how severe. The pool game started with the biggest bet at hand. It all came down to the 8-ball for both. But it was Aaron’s turn. Samantha failed to pocket it, which troubled her. Aaron knew it was an intermediate shot. Required some skill to pocket but understandable if he misses. It all came down to that one shot. On one side was integrity, morale and his best friend cum associate. On the other, his desire for a successful career, and a huge firm. It was all upto him. Whether the shot was intentional or not, he still does not know. A midnight bell rang in the distance. And he took the shot. The 8 ball went in. Samantha’s consequence in her own words was” I can’t…. stay in this firm anymore, I just can’t. You are not the partner I expected..anymore.” and she ran out crying in the darkness. Aaron had never felt so lonely in his life. Samantha’s role in his life was one that even he failed to understand. But now that it was gone, he felt empty as if someone took a part of his soul. He wandered off into a pub and realized after a few drinks that he hadn’t felt so close to success in his life either. He decided to move on, forceful and depressing though it maybe, it seemed only the next logical step. The next day, he briefed Todd who seemed to take forging a document an activity like getting his car washed. Just something you have to do regularly. But nothing could stop Aaron now. The court date arrived next week and Aaron’s law skills spread throughout the city. He was now a big-time lawyer. He took huge cases, ranging from criminal cases: defending criminals to keep his pocket full and pro bono: to give him the fabricated feeling from time to time that he is still doing good for the community. He tried to contact Samantha a few times, but with no avail. He never realized the severe consequences she warned him about were not over. Cut to present. Last year, he had learned that Zargenzy was still in hiding, and he did not like the fact that a small lawyer named Aaron Walker had made sure that his overseas stay was more than difficult and long. And that worthless insect Todd Gleeson was running the company. Aaron had received an email threatening his law firm, “Walker & Co. is about to blow” summed it up, because the heat on Zargenzy had lessened. Slowly over the year, Aaron witnessed the epidemic that took over his firm. Employees quit with a look of fear in their eyes, they stopped winning cases and the word around town went from “Walker&Co. is the best” to “Walker&Co., is that a beer company?” He realized he had lost. Todd Gleeson had fallen to his death from a bridge while walking due to a ‘knee health issue’. There was no way he was going to beat Zargenzy at this game. He emailed him back, at the same email address, inviting him to his original firm location. Which he had never bothered to sell. Actually, he just couldn’t part with it. He wrote another e-mail to Samantha inviting her as well, but at an earlier time. He had to see her once, he had to know, he had to tell, he had to accept the fact that he gave up his partner for a lonely successful life. He had to see her. But there was no R.S.V.P. And this is how Aaron arrived at his old office, after nearly 15 years. Maybe Samantha wasn’t coming or she was late. In any case, the last memory he will have of her will be her rushing out leaving a teardrop trail behind. Him sitting down and crying consequently. Because then entered Steve Zargenzy. Before Aaron could even reach for his compact handgun and try to distract him with his lawyer pleasantries, he was shot, thrice. They say that your whole life flashes in front of you before you die, especially the moments with people you cherish most. He saw his family but the most distinct memory was of arguing over legalizing marijuana with Samantha, while being high on marijuana. He saw a memory of her hair flying in the wind. He wondered, what if? Aaron didn’t mind the outcome. With his career nearly destroyed and his loneliness eating him up from inside, he had nothing to live for. He was happy to have passed in his ‘genèse’. It felt poetic. What he didn’t see was the two green eyes peeking through the window, now with a more emerald glow which added a sort of wisdom. After witnessing the murder of her former best friend, Samantha walked away. Tears welled up in her eyes, but no action took form in her head. She thought of husband, her two kids and her small but satisfying law firm. Some may call it fear. But after all, isn’t everyone a little greedy? Aaron always thought, what if Samantha hadn’t pursued the squirrel? What if its tail wasn’t dwindling so sweetly? Would they have still been partners? Aaron always knew the answer was no. Someday, another offer would have come up, tempting him even more and then even Samantha’s logic would fail. The two were like the ends of a compressed spring, waiting to be pushed apart. Ideology can create barriers. But another thought used to strike his mind was the possibility of one conforming to the mindset of the other, by the time the next offer comes. But how much time? They were on the brink of shutting down. They needed the money and Aaron realized that. What if they had bought the Mayan? It would have radiated a more elegant and classy feel to the rugged office. Maybe the Mayan would have knocked some sense into Aaron, instead the pool table provided just a path to the apparently ‘ethically inappropriate’ way. They could have sold the statue to an artifact collector with some schemed lies for quick money.. Thing is, Aaron never knew the cunning side of Samantha even after all the years together. He didn’t know what would be considered crossing the line according to her. People always try to put up their best in front of people,even their best friends. One could also argue the flexibility of Aaron’s incentive and decision when he took the shot. What if he had let Samantha win on purpose. They would have remained together, forever, because not Aaron nor Samantha would have lost that match, it would be the greedy devil inside Aaron getting demolished in the battle. What if, and this was Aaron’s deepest secret which even he didn’t know of, what if he could have thrown the 8 ball and the cue ball away, slid across the table and kissed Samantha, saying “ I love you and your integrity”? What would have been her response? What if? title: Defeated
author: Unknown
preview: I feel like a prophet of my own tragedies. When I gamble my odds between love and pain, my prophecy wins and my soul loses. I am so desperate to be happy that my frantic jitters kick all the bliss away. I have lived so m...

blocks.content: I feel like a prophet of my own tragedies.
When I gamble my odds between love and pain,
my prophecy wins and my soul loses.
I am so desperate to be happy that my frantic jitters kick all the bliss away.
I have lived so much in the dark that the light that I seek burns my eyes all the way to within.
I sometimes think I know a way to revert this but I don’t.
I am too ugly for love, in all ways.
On my voyage to find happiness, all I get in return are the hurts I had buried away.
It’s easier to be lonely when you’re alone.
But it hurts much more to be lonely among people, content and complete.
I want to walk, no I want to float away from everyone else.
Don’t know where
But somewhere.
I am tired of trying so hard to win in this losing game.
I just want to lose now.

title: Faded
author: Unknown
preview: I shoveled a slice of a sandwich down my throat, burned my taste buds with hot milk and came out of the hall to zombie my way to the class. It was a long walk with no music in my ears to amuse. That, I feared, would leav...

blocks.content: I shoveled a slice of a sandwich down my throat, burned my taste buds with hot milk and came out of the hall to zombie my way to the class. It was a long walk with no music in my ears to amuse. That, I feared, would leave my mind warbling into melancholic symphonies of thoughts reminding me reasons to feel dejected. And it did; my parents were coming to meet me because I had avoided going home for too long. I was sure it wasn’t out of concern. It was just their whim to prize a chance to condemn the free will I happened to use and teach me life lessons they did not follow themselves. I did not want to sit alone; I thought when I imagined my 8 AM class filled with people looking at their phones after getting frustrated from the fugly board work and professor’s irksome habit of repeating everything twice. Who would I sit next to? Who could I sit next to? Should I sit next to Anmol? He was probably more comfortable with that wing mate of his. Besides, I might say one too many jokes to repel him, either at his expense or his friend’s. Should I sit next to Karan and Saksham? Saksham would pass some remark on my annoying face or the apparent blight of my existence. Should I sit next to Priyal? She talks nicely to me online, but I don’t want to scare her off with this persona of a forlorn freak. She wouldn’t ever understand the afflictions behind these wide, bright foolish grins and it would end abysmally even if she did. Tragedies were an expense that I couldn’t afford in those hard times, at least not for her. I decided to sit with strangers and focus on the class instead. With wounds of the recent mid-semester test afresh, I witnessed my will to learn to build up and but it got down gradually as the uninspiring lecture about something even more uninspiring, wrapped in South Indian accent and semantic errors, continued maintaining its consistency of boredom. After the class, I joined Karan and Saksham in CCD where I tried to study but ended up engaged in their rants about the pointlessness of technical arts courses. I did not say anything. I did not wish to talk at all for some reason that day. Even when I wanted to say anything, I would realize immediately that my words felt cozier and more revered in my head than out in the outside world, full of eyes and frowns dancing around them. Sheera arrived soon after. “Is he still missing?” She asked looking at us. Strangely, she did not even glance at me though she was one of the few people who did not hate me, even when I was busy being the bitterest of an asshole. “It’s quite unfortunate. What do you think happened?” Karan questioned but not in an inquisitive demeanor. I could sense they were expecting the inevitable, but none of them wanted to be the one to say it loud. Karan then told us how the boy’s parents were consistently calling everyone including him. It was one of the people of their friend’s circle. Karan looked worried. Others, a tad less. I, however, had no worries because I did not belong to that circle. They made sure of that by not inviting me to their outings. It wasn’t their fault. Or at least it wasn’t theirs as much as it was everyone else’s since there was supposedly no flock where my feathers belonged. “Hasn’t there been another one in Girls’ Hostel? I heard someone saying something about a missing girl.” Oh no . I had made a guess. I needed to know her name. “Do you know who she is?”, Saksham asked before I could. “N..”. The sound of ‘N” was enough for me. I knew her, well enough to not want to hear someone say her name. We both had found a far cry in this institute, a seemingly unfathomed ocean of opportunities bound by four walls, filled underneath with preys and predators of hopelessness and shattered dreams. Nothing appealed to me deep down. Maths was too high up its ass. Competitive coding was too competitive. My branch was too predictable and uninteresting. The drive was gone. The fire was gone. I had tried to light it back up by trying to feel for a face and to make that face care for me, but mine wasn’t pretty enough to fool someone with something false, or even with something true. I hadn’t talked to her much, but I had sensed that same exhaustion of trying everything and failing nonetheless in those severe eyes below those low blase brows. I did see both of us as the grits thrown out from between the wheels of this larva of a society. I considered looking for her. It wasn’t for any infatuation. She wasn’t the beautiful-dateable type. She looked more like the one you’d live with, in a post-apocalyptic world and fuck before going out to hunt for food or oil or something. But that’s not the point. Both of us had seen something dark and bizarre that lurked somewhere the corners of our eyes end between our minds begin. Because of that and a strange feeling of the gut, I decided to give it a try. I was at the front gate of GH(girls’ hostel) when I realized I had not brought my identity card with me to pass through the guard. I took my chances by sneaking into the group of friends that I had hung out with, in the first winter. After successfully getting through, I quickly left them without any chat and took the elevator. Elevator took some long restless seconds to get to the top floor. I tried to hold back my loud anxiety growing as the door opened. I controlled my breath and pumped my fist hoping it would slow down my heart while pacing towards her room. The door lay wide open as everything stood silent and still in the room, undeterred by the wind and dust from the balcony. The evening seemed to grow bluer and more silent when I observed tranquil shrill screams dropping with sobs from the verandah. “Why?” A whisper escaped, or I thought it did. I stepped onto the balcony. In the corner, with messed up hair, thighs relaxing in an unshy way and tear-filled eyes fixed on me as I looked at her, there she was. We both looked confused. “Please tell me you can see me.” “What?” “Shit, you can see me. How?” “Wait, what? What do you mean?” “Something’s wrong. No one can see me. No one can hear me. Am I a ghost? I don’t know what’s happening. It’s worse than death; it would be…”, she looked at me with a frown and looked away outside. I didn’t know whether or how to comfort her. I wanted to calm her shoulders and give her a warm hug, but I held myself back with apprehension and confusion. The reasonable answer cued mental instability. How else could it be explained? An answer came into my mind. The thing we tried running away from, looked right back at me in a flash at the back of my eyelids. Wait . I reflected on my day. I slowly left the room without drawing back her attention. I stared at the guard as I passed straight through the gate. Something appalling struck my mind. I ignored that thought and looked at my watch. My parents would have arrived by now. I was going to hear more of their “emphasized knowledge” for not calling them to ask about their whereabouts and wellbeing during their journey. I was outside my room bracing myself and mentally preparing to explain to them that I am okay and trying not to hammer my head to the wall while they’d keep repeating their same old sermons with more belligerence each time. I opened the door. My roommate was out. And my dad was standing while my mom was sitting on my bed. They were discussing how my elder brother was continuing to mess up his life and bringing them shame. They did not notice me. That thought came back haunting. I stood between them. They did not stop. Now I knew who the guy who had gone missing was. It was me. Figures . Unheard and unseen, caught between those hateful disses from my parents, I realized that my existence had finally faded. Indeed it was worse than death. With an exhale, I went back out where the bright day had ended and imperceptible night had risen. I glanced through the footpaths. There were people so many. None I knew. I might have known a few, but there wasn’t one soul that understood me nor was there someone I understood. Far away, I saw her again. We looked at each other. Desperation escaped through my face. She rolled her eyes to the left and looked back again. Sympathy died as apprehension kicked in. We both turned our back and went our ways. I peeked at her again while walking away. She had faded away for me as well. Perhaps, I too had, for her. I kept waiting for the moment when I would vanish away from myself. title: Dreamer on the Train
author: Unknown
preview: It was raining heavily back home. Drip, Drip, Drop. It’d been hours, and she was there, waiting at the station. The train was late and apparently, she was the only one who didn’t get the information on time. All alone, w...

blocks.content: It was raining heavily back home.
Drip, Drip, Drop.

It’d been hours, and she was there, waiting at the station. The train was late and apparently, she was the only one who didn’t get the information on time. All alone, with the station-master and a few regular people as an exception, sitting in the lounge, with her iPad, her books, her stories, she starts to drift away.

The bench had become warm by now, but the air seemed to talk to her bones, chilling them to their core as if it carried with itself horror stories from another dimension. She took off her coat and pulled it in front of her, in a desperate attempt to close the listening aids of her bones, in a negligibly effective move to avoid the air from hitting her.

She looks above, the skies are dark as if it’s London in the old days, or a romantic movie perhaps, with the rain and all, and a couple in the middle of the path with the view grey as it is, becoming coloured only where they stood. Hopefully it wasn’t the rail-track where they expressed their affection for it might mean the end of their love story as she was expecting the train any time now.*Giggle*
“Excuse me miss. I’ve been want-‘”
“Wha-“, she was startled at the voice of another soul. She didn’t hear any footsteps, or maybe it was just the rain hid them as curtains do light.

“I was saying, would you be so kind as to tell me what you are doing at this time of the hour over here at the train station? A little girl like you shouldn’t be alone around these areas. Where are your parents?”
She sharpened her gaze and tried to look more clearly, to identify that the station master had come over. Probably his shift got over and was concerned about her.
“Oh! I was waiting for a train. My parents have gone back to where they belong, Mister-?”
“Joshua. I’d say, what has this world come up to, letting a young lady such as yourself all alone at night over a place such as this. What about those goons that roam around here?”
“Well, I can take care of myself quite well you see. There’s nothing to be worried about. Thank you for your concern though.”
“If you say so, I’ll be on my way. Take care!”, the station-master departed.

Little Asha sat there by herself, all through the night till the morning when the train arrived, wondering about how fake the world is, like the station-master, pretending to care while all of it is just a way to tell to themselves how good they are. ‘Puh! If he was so nice, then why didn’t he stay the night, giving me company?’, she thought.
The train did arrive, and quite late one would say, but there was one thing off when it departed, Asha was not on it.
